newsitem.title: JAPAN: Foreigners net buyers of Japanese stocks in month.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners net buyers of Japanese stocks in month.

text.p: Foreigners were net buyers of Japanese stocks on the Tokyo, Osaka and Nagoya stock exchanges in the month from April 28 to May 30, exchange data showed.

Market sources said although there was support from pension funds and dealers, foreign investors played a large role in helping to boost the Nikkei average, which climbed nearly eight percent during the period.
"U.S. stocks have been steaming higher, pulling other stock markets except for Tokyo with them," a "Big Four" broker said.
"Japanese stocks, which were battered severely in early January, were still bargains in comparison (to other markets)," he said.
The Nikkei average tumbled to 17,303.65 on January 10, the lowest since the low of 16,916.57 posted on August 14, 1995.
Brokers added that as the 225-share Nikkei had risen considerably from the level of 18,003.40 it ended the 1996/97 business year on, domestic institutional investors were busy locking in profits.

"The upturn in Japanese stocks is also encouraging for companies seeking to dispose of their cross shareholdings," an analyst at a second-tier brokerage said. "But up until now, foreign investor purchases have been able to offset the losses and the selling has gone relatively unnoticed."
In May, Tokyo bourse data showed that investment trusts, companies and financial institutions were net sellers of stocks by 0.58 trillion yen.
Private investors were also net sellers by 0.31 trillion yen. Dealers, however, were net buyers by 0.06 trillion yen.
